text: What Mistral is Mistral AI is a Paris lab founded in April 2023 by Arthur Mensch (from Google DeepMind) and Guillaume Lample and Timothée Lacroix (both from Meta) ( Wikipedia ).
label: core

text: It is the European counterweight to the Chinese labs that lead open weights, alongside Ai2 and the Institute of Foundation Models (the page's own positioning, not a sourced ranking) .
label: core

text: Its strategy is a bet that a cheaper model with open weights and EU jurisdiction wins the deals that raw benchmark position does not: sovereign and defence deployments, regulated on-premises installs, and anyone who cannot legally send tokens to a US API.
label: core

text: Mensch put the capability position plainly in July 2026: "we do not yet own the best language models, but we've constantly reduced that gap" ( Tech Times ).
label: core

text: Technically it is a fast follower rather than an originator.
label: core

text: It takes an efficiency idea that already works (sliding-window attention, grouped-query attention, sparse mixture of experts, and in 2025 DeepSeek's latent attention) and has repeatedly been early to ship it at a size people can run on their own hardware: Mistral 7B in September 2023, then Mixtral 8x7B a few months later, which made open sparse mixture-of-experts models mainstream.
label: core
key: ships it early at a size people can run

text: Two things are distinctively Mistral, and the rest of this page is about them: The shapes it chose: a 4,096-token window over 32 layers, 32 query heads sharing 8 key-value heads, eight big experts, and now 128 small ones ( Mistral 7B , Mixtral , Current line ).
label: core

text: A licence ladder from Apache 2.0 to API only, which decides what you may do with each model more than any benchmark does ( Licences ).
label: core

text: The generic mechanisms are owned elsewhere and summarised here only as far as this page needs them: mixture-of-experts routing, load balancing and expert parallelism on Mixture of experts ; grouped-query and sliding-window attention across the field, and how to read a KV-cache figure, on LLM Architecture Gallery ; reasoning modes on Topic: llm-landscape (Deeper: test-time compute) .
label: core

section: mistral 7b: a sliding window and shared key-value heads
text: A decoder's KV cache holds the keys and values every past token leaves behind for attention to read.
label: owned:models_and_training/topic_llm_architecture/long_context

section: mistral 7b: a sliding window and shared key-value heads
text: It grows with every token, and at decode time reading it is the bottleneck: decoding is limited by memory bandwidth rather than arithmetic, so a smaller cache turns directly into larger batches and more tokens per second on the same GPU.
label: owned:models_and_training/topic_llm_architecture/long_context

section: mistral 7b: a sliding window and shared key-value heads
text: Mistral 7B attacked the cache twice at once: it limits how many past tokens each layer may attend to, and it lets several query heads share one set of keys and values.
label: core

section: mistral 7b: a sliding window and shared key-value heads
text: Each layer attends only to the last W tokens, with W = 4,096 , so the cache never needs more than W positions.
label: core

section: mistral 7b: a sliding window and shared key-value heads
text: Mistral implemented it as a rolling buffer : position i is written to slot i mod W , overwriting the token that just fell out of the window, so the cache is a fixed-size ring rather than a growing list.
label: core

section: mistral 7b: a sliding window and shared key-value heads
text: Information still travels further than W because windows stack: layer 2 at position i reads layer-1 states that already summarise the W tokens before them, so after k layers a token can be influenced by roughly k · W earlier tokens, the way a stack of small convolutions builds a large receptive field.
label: core

section: mistral 7b: a sliding window and shared key-value heads
text: The price: anything beyond the window arrives only through what the intermediate states carried forward, so exact long-range recall is weaker than with full attention.
label: core

section: mistral 7b: a sliding window and shared key-value heads
text: Mistral itself dropped the window in Mixtral, which supports "a fully dense context length of 32k tokens" ( Mixtral paper ); the field later settled on mixing windowed and full layers, covered on the LLM Architecture Gallery page.
label: core
key: a fully dense context length of 32k tokens

section: mistral 7b: a sliding window and shared key-value heads
text: 32 query heads but only 8 key-value heads, so each group of 4 query heads reads the same keys and values.
label: core

section: mistral 7b: a sliding window and shared key-value heads
text: The cache stores 8 heads per layer instead of 32, a quarter of what full multi-head attention (MHA) would store.
label: core
key: a quarter of what multi-head attention

text: The shape ( Mistral 7B paper , Table 1; config.json ): model width 4,096, 32 layers, head dimension 128, feed-forward width 14,336, 32 query heads, 8 key-value heads, window 4,096, context length 8,192, vocabulary 32,000, Apache 2.0.

section: mistral 7b: a sliding window and shared key-value heads
text: It outperformed "the best open 13B model (Llama 2) across all evaluated benchmarks, and the best released 34B model (Llama 1) in reasoning, mathematics, and code generation" ( paper ), which is what established the lab, and it became a common small base for fine-tuning (unconfirmed as "the default") .
label: core

section: mistral 7b: a sliding window and shared key-value heads
text: Worked example: Mistral 7B's cache at 32,768 tokens Bytes per token: 2 × 32 × 8 × 128 × 2 = 131,072 bytes, 128 KiB.
label: core

section: mistral 7b: a sliding window and shared key-value heads
text: Without the window, 32,768 tokens cost 32,768 × 128 KiB = 4 GiB .
label: core

section: mistral 7b: a sliding window and shared key-value heads
text: With the rolling buffer only min(32,768, 4,096) = 4,096 positions are held: 4,096 × 128 KiB = 512 MiB , eight times less: "On a sequence length of 32k tokens, this reduces the cache memory usage by 8x, without impacting the model quality" ( paper ).
label: core
key: reduces the cache memory usage by 8x

section: mistral 7b: a sliding window and shared key-value heads
text: With full multi-head attention ( n kv = 32 ) and no window, four times step 2: 16 GiB, more than the model's own weights (about 14.5 GB at 16 bits).
label: core
key: more than the model's own 14.5 gb

section: mistral 7b: a sliding window and shared key-value heads
text: Reach at the last layer: 32 × 4,096 = 131,072 tokens, the paper's "theoretical attention span of approximately 131K tokens", sixteen times the 8,192-token context the model was trained on.
label: core

section: mistral 7b: a sliding window and shared key-value heads
text: The two savings multiply: GQA divides the per-token cost by 4, the window caps the number of tokens, and at 32k together they hold the cache to 512 MiB against 16 GiB, a factor of 32.
label: core

section: mixtral: mistral 7b with eight feed-forward networks
text: Mixtral: Mistral 7B with eight feed-forward networks Mixtral 8x7B (December 2023) is Mistral 7B's block with one change that mattered and one that is easy to miss ( Mixtral paper ; config.json ).
label: core

section: mixtral: mistral 7b with eight feed-forward networks
text: The change that mattered: each layer's feed-forward network becomes 8 expert networks of the same shape plus a router that sends every token to the top 2, mixing their outputs by the router's weights (a softmax over the two kept scores).
label: core
key: sends every token to the top 2

section: mixtral: mistral 7b with eight feed-forward networks
text: The one easy to miss: it dropped the sliding window for full attention over 32k tokens.
label: core
key: dropped the sliding window for full attention

section: mixtral: mistral 7b with eight feed-forward networks
text: Everything else (width 4,096, 32 layers, 32 query and 8 key-value heads) is Mistral 7B's.
label: core

section: mixtral: mistral 7b with eight feed-forward networks
text: That is why "8x7B" is about 47B parameters, not 56B: only the feed-forward networks are copied; attention and embeddings are shared.

section: mixtral: mistral 7b with eight feed-forward networks

text: First, Mixtral "outperforms or matches Llama 2 70B and GPT-3.5 across all evaluated benchmarks" at the per-token compute of a 13B model, under Apache 2.0 ( paper ), which is what made open sparse models mainstream.

section: mixtral: mistral 7b with eight feed-forward networks
text: Second, its routing analysis found experts do not specialise by topic: expert distributions over ArXiv, PubMed, PhilPapers and the rest of The Pile are nearly identical, and the router shows "structured syntactic behavior", so tokens such as self in Python or "Question" in English "often get routed through the same expert".
label: core

section: mixtral: mistral 7b with eight feed-forward networks
text: Consecutive tokens are assigned the same expert far more often than chance in the middle and late layers, which matters for load balancing (a hot pair of experts can over-subscribe one GPU) and can be exploited for caching: First choice repeats First or second choice overlaps Share of consecutive tokens given the same expert, by layer and dataset, from the Mixtral paper , Table 5.

text: The specialist years, 2024 to 2025.
label: core
key: in 2024 and 2025 mistral shipped a model per job

text: A flagship that started API-only (Mistral Large 1, February 2024; Large 2 in July 2024 released its weights under the research-only Mistral Research License, with a paid licence for commercial self-deployment, Mistral ) and price tiers (Small 3 and 3.1 back on Apache 2.0, Medium 3 on the API), plus a model per job: Codestral for code, trained for fill-in-the-middle so it completes inside a file given both the prefix and the suffix, the shape editor autocomplete needs; Ministral edge models; Pixtral for vision (from September 2024), an image encoder feeding the language decoder so images and text interleave in one context; Voxtral for speech understanding (July 2025); Magistral (June 2025), Mistral's first reasoning models; and Devstral (May 2025) for agentic coding, tuned for the loop of reading a repository, editing files and running tests inside a scaffold rather than emitting one code block.
label: core

text: Mistral 3 (2 December 2025): Large 3 plus Ministral 3 at 3B, 8B and 14B, each in base, instruct and reasoning variants, all multimodal and Apache 2.0; Mistral reports 85% on AIME 2025 for the 14B reasoning variant ( Mistral ).
label: core

text: Devstral 2 and Devstral Small 2 followed a week later with the Vibe command-line coding agent.
label: core

text: The specialists folded back into generalists: Small 4 (March) absorbed Magistral and Devstral behind a reasoning setting, and Medium 3.5 (April, announced in May) replaced Magistral and Devstral 2 in Mistral's own products.
label: core

text: Vision is now built into Large 3, Small 4 and Medium 3.5, and every Pixtral, Magistral and Devstral version is in the deprecated table of Mistral's catalogue .
label: core

text: Specialists remain where the job is different in kind: speech (Voxtral TTS, March, open weights under a non-commercial licence; the Voxtral transcription models), document OCR (OCR 4 in June, replaced by OCR 4.1 in July), formal proofs ( Leanstral ), safety ( Shieldstral , August) and robotics ( Robostral Navigate , July).
label: core

text: How Mistral trains Mistral publishes weights first and papers rarely, so most of its recipes have to be inferred from the artefacts.
label: core
key: publishes weights first and papers rarely

text: Two things are documented, both in the Magistral paper .
label: core

text: Distillation from its own larger models.
label: core

text: Magistral Small (24B, Apache 2.0) was cold-started with supervised fine-tuning of Mistral Small 3 on reasoning traces from Magistral Medium (correct traces from Medium's RL run, plus Medium's answers to OpenThoughts and OpenR1 code prompts, plus 10% general instruction data), then trained with reinforcement learning on top.
label: core

text: That is distillation in the ordinary sense: the small model learns from the large one's outputs rather than from raw data alone.
label: fat
note: wind-up, restatement, control labels or a pointer to a removed tab

text: Magistral's RL recipe , the one place the lab was genuinely open about method.
label: fat
note: wind-up, restatement, control labels or a pointer to a removed tab

text: Magistral Medium was trained from Mistral Medium 3 by pure reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR): no learned reward model, and no reasoning traces distilled from someone else's reasoner.
label: core
key: reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (rlvr) alone

text: A rollout is scored by mechanically checking its final answer (a maths result by a rule-based checker with SymPy, or code against 20 unit tests), so style cannot game the reward the way it can game a preference model.
label: core

text: The algorithm is GRPO (Group Relative Policy Optimisation: sample a group of answers to one prompt and score each against the group's mean instead of a learned critic; the full objective is on RL for LLMs: RLHF, GRPO, RLVR ), with Mistral's own changes: No KL penalty to the starting model, so the policy may move as far as the reward pulls it; Mistral found the policy diverges regardless and the reference copy was not worth its compute.
label: owned:models_and_training/topic_llm_training_and_post_training/alignment_sft_rlhf_dpo_rlvr

text: Clip-higher: the upper clipping threshold ε high raised so rare but useful tokens can gain probability faster: tuned between 0.26 and 0.28 for Medium, 0.3 for Small.
label: core

text: For scale, PPO's original setting is 0.2 on both sides ( PPO paper ); the Magistral paper does not state its lower bound.
label: core

text: A token at probability 0.01 may rise to 0.0128 in one update at 0.28, against 0.012 at 0.2.
label: core

text: Length-normalised loss over all tokens of all answers in a group, so long answers do not dominate; the advantage is simply r i − μ (no division by the group's spread), normalised again across each minibatch.
label: core

text: Zero-advantage filtering: groups where every answer got the same reward carry no learning signal and are dropped from the batch.
label: core

text: Reward: 0 if the format is wrong (one <think> block, the answer in \boxed{} or a fenced code block); otherwise 0.1 for the format, a further 0.9 for a correct answer, a soft length penalty of up to −0.1 that grows linearly once an answer passes l max − l cache (raised from 16k to 32k tokens during Medium's run), and 0.1 more when the problem, the reasoning and the answer are all in the same language (10% of problems were translated into French, Spanish, Italian, German, Chinese and Russian).
label: core

text: Try: one group of eight answers to the same problem.

key: does not state the group size

text: Standard GRPO divides by the group's standard deviation; Magistral does not, and normalises across the minibatch instead.

text: Common mistakes and misconceptions "Mistral models use sliding-window attention." Mistral 7B did; Mixtral, a few months later, already used full attention over 32k, and the current models use full grouped-query or latent attention.
label: core
key: a 2023 mistral choice, not a family trait

text: Treat SWA as a 2023 Mistral choice, not a family trait. "8x7B means 56B parameters." Only the feed-forward networks are replicated; attention and embeddings are shared, so it is 46.7B total and 12.9B active. "Mixtral's experts are topic experts." Mistral's own routing analysis found syntactic rather than topical specialisation, and strong repetition between consecutive tokens. "Everything Mistral ships is Apache 2.0." Medium 3.5 and Devstral 2 are under a modified MIT licence with a $20M monthly revenue exception, Voxtral TTS is non-commercial, and Codestral, OCR and the embedding models have no public weights. "Magistral is Mistral's reasoning model." It was; reasoning is now a setting on Small 4 and Medium 3.5, and every Magistral version is deprecated in the catalogue. "Magistral was all pure RL." Magistral Medium was; Magistral Small started from Magistral Medium's traces. "The 131K reach means Mistral 7B handles 131K-token inputs." It is a theoretical bound on how far information can propagate through 32 windowed layers; the model was trained on 8,192-token contexts. "Large 3 is a scaled-up Mixtral." Its configuration is DeepSeek-V3's skeleton, latent attention and a shared expert included, with 128 experts instead of 256.
